clue.text: Element identified by many in Rome once

definitions.text: Element identified by many in Rome once

parts.words: Element identified by many in Rome once
parts.note: the chemical element whose symbol is the same letter the ancient Romans used for a hundred, so 'many' in Roman numerals names it

explanation.surface: A puzzle about some element that crowds of ancient Romans could recognise.
explanation.walkthrough: The element's chemical symbol is C, and C is the Roman numeral for 100, the 'many' of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the chemical element with symbol C, the basis of all organic compounds.

clue.text: A quiet one certainly, but fast.

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for soft or quiet
an ace counts as one in cards and dice

explanation.surface: A quiet person, though certainly a quick one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'certainly, but' are link words; the pieces are A, P (piano, quiet) and ACE (one).
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old adverb meaning quickly, at speed.

clue.text: An engagement to alert both involved

indicators.note: something involved is tangled up, so the letters of the words before it are mixed

explanation.surface: A wedding announcement that should put both families on notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A betrothal is a formal promise to marry, an engagement.

clue.text: Mean about very small measure of drink

indicators.note: about says the word for mean goes round the measure

parts.note: near is old slang for stingy or mean
ct is short for carat, a tiny unit of weight for gems

explanation.surface: A stingy host pours only a tiny tot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' is stingy, NEAR, not an average; 'about' wraps it round CT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar is the mythical drink of the gods, and by extension any delicious beverage.

clue.text: Not brave, like a theatrical Knight?

parts.note: Sir Noel Coward, the playwright and actor, was knighted in 1970
the suffix -ly turns a noun into a word meaning 'like' it

explanation.surface: Someone timid, compared to a stage actor who has been knighted.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel Coward was a famous British playwright and performer, Sir Noel from 1970; adding the suffix LY ('like') gives a word that sounds like a description of his manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking courage is the plain sense of the word; a timid person shrinks from danger.

clue.text: Guests see artist perform jumps here in America

parts.note: co is short for company, the guests one has round
lo is an old word meaning look or see
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
to do is to perform
springs means jumps or leaps

explanation.surface: Visitors watch a painter put on a show of leaps somewhere in the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is the stock crossword artist; 'here in America' points at a US place.
explanation.definitionFit: Colorado Springs is a city in the US state of Colorado, so it is a place in America.

clue.text: Combat uniform for a female 22

parts.note: war is armed combat
dress is the clothing worn on duty, as in mess dress

explanation.surface: Battle fatigues for a woman prison officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 down is SCREW, British slang for a prison officer, so a female one is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardress is a woman prison guard, and prisoners call guards by that slang word.

clue.text: Pictorial representation of military transport

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a bus is a means of transport

explanation.surface: A drawing of an army vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a puzzle that stands for words with pictures and symbols.

clue.text: Making a filthy profit?

parts.note: plays on the phrase 'filthy lucre', money thought of as dirty

explanation.surface: Earning money by dishonest or dirty means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filthy lucre' is an old phrase for money, so something that makes lucre is profitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that brings in a good deal of money is profitable, generating large gains.

clue.text: In which the House of Peers did nothing very well? (Gilbert)

definitions.text: In which the House of Peers did nothing very well? (Gilbert)

parts.words: In which the House of Peers did nothing very well? (Gilbert)
parts.note: a line from W S Gilbert's Iolanthe says the House of Peers 'did nothing in' a certain way, 'and did it very well'

explanation.surface: A quiz question about a line in a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta.
explanation.walkthrough: In Gilbert and Sullivan's Iolanthe the song 'When Britain really ruled the waves' says the House of Peers did nothing in this word, and did it very well.
explanation.definitionFit: The quoted lyric completes the phrase 'nothing in ...', meaning nothing specific or special.

clue.text: Dollar for a dandy

definitions.meaning: an old word for a fashionable young man about town

explanation.surface: A dollar spent to dress a fop.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a US dollar and also an old term for a fashionable, showy young man.

clue.text: Carefree and of good French appearance

parts.note: de is French for 'of'
bon is the French word for good
an air is a look or manner someone gives off

explanation.surface: Someone relaxed who also looks fine in a French way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' governs 'of good', giving DE BON; AIR is English for an appearance, and the phrase de bon air, 'of good bearing', is where the word comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: A debonair person is jaunty and untroubled, at ease and light-hearted in manner.

clue.text: Lascar rogue

indicators.note: a rogue element behaves wildly, so the letters of the word before it are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: An Indian seaman who turns out to be a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: A lascar is a sailor from India or South-East Asia; its letters, gone 'rogue', rearrange to the answer, and a roguish lascar is just what the whole clue describes.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel or mischievous person is a rogue; a lascar behaving badly is such a person.

clue.text: Thin coat for artist in rough water

definitions.meaning: a thin layer of diluted paint or ink laid over a picture
the disturbed water left behind a moving boat

explanation.surface: A painter puts on a thin layer while out on choppy seas.
explanation.definitionFit: Painters lay a thin diluted coat of colour, and the same word names the churned water behind a boat.

clue.text: He catalogues the record this vicar made

indicators.note: made means the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A clergyman's written history is filed by a records keeper.
explanation.definitionFit: This person keeps and catalogues historical documents and records.

clue.text: A woman's characteristic to be absent-minded

parts.note: Di, short for Diana, is a woman's name; with the 's it gives DIS
a trait is a distinguishing characteristic

explanation.surface: Being forgetful is said to be a typical female quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French, it describes someone distracted, inattentive and lost in thought.

clue.text: Displaying indignation, though calm about some points

indicators.note: about says the word for calm goes round the points

parts.note: restful means calm and peaceful
E and N, east and north, are points of the compass

explanation.surface: Being cross even though one stays calm on certain issues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' are compass points, E and N; 'about' puts RESTFUL round them.
explanation.definitionFit: A resentful person shows bitter displeasure at being treated unfairly.

clue.text: Found in a teacup it's comparatively odd

definitions.meaning: folklore says a tea leaf floating in a cup foretells the arrival of a newcomer, called by this name
more odd, the comparative of a word for odd

explanation.surface: Something in a cup of tea is rather peculiar.
explanation.walkthrough: In British tea-leaf folklore, a leaf or stalk floating in your tea means a visitor is coming, and that floating leaf is given this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A floating tea leaf is said to foretell an unknown visitor, and the word also means more unusual.

clue.text: Attendants replaced by Colet, say

indicators.note: replaced means the letters of the following words are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: Some servants have been swapped out by a school founder, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR gave 'Colt', but the page prints 'Colet' (John Colet founded St Paul's School); 'replaced' rearranges COLET SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acolytes are assistants who serve a priest at the altar, so attendants or followers.

clue.text: Subject of Phidias's statue returned to this port

indicators.note: returned says the god's name is read back to front

parts.note: Phidias carved the great statue of Zeus at Olympia, one of the Seven Wonders

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek sculpture is sent back to an Egyptian harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: Phidias's statue of Zeus at Olympia was a wonder of the ancient world; 'returned' turns ZEUS round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian town at the southern end of its canal is a busy harbour.

clue.text: Greek character stuck in a stoppage shows charm

indicators.note: stuck in says the Greek letter sits inside the other words

parts.note: a let is a hindrance or obstruction, as in 'without let or hindrance'
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person caught in a hold-up reveals some appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charm' is the noun, a lucky charm, not attractiveness; 'shows' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is an object worn as a talisman against evil, a lucky charm.

clue.text: Unhealthy atmosphere a feature of Hermia's marriage

indicators.note: feature of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Gloom hangs over the wedding of Hermia from A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasma is a noxious vapour or oppressive air once thought to spread disease.

clue.text: Worn-out horse for a miser

definitions.meaning: an old broken-down horse, a nag

explanation.surface: An old nag for a skinflint.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a broken-down horse and also for a tight-fisted person.

clue.text: "Don't forget to deliver 'on both sides of the motorway"

indicators.note: one word placed on both sides of another wraps right round it

parts.note: to render is to give or deliver
the M1 is Britain's first and best-known motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A note telling someone to make a delivery along the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the main London-to-Leeds motorway, MI in crosswords; 'on both sides of' puts RENDER round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A note saying 'Don't forget' is a prompt to remember something.

clue.text: Two measures for the lake lady

parts.note: an ell is an old cloth measure; an en is a printer's measure
an ell is an old cloth measure; an en is a printer's measure

explanation.surface: Two units of length for a woman by the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Ellen Douglas is the heroine of Walter Scott's poem The Lady of the Lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Scott's heroine in The Lady of the Lake bears this name.

clue.text: Seaside attraction for 'the more devout?

definitions.meaning: a seaside promenade structure built out over the sea

explanation.surface: A holiday resort feature that appeals to churchgoers.
explanation.definitionFit: Resorts have long jetties with amusements, and 'pi' is old slang for pious, so 'pi-er' is the more devout.

clue.text: Mild sort of music for those of good birth

parts.note: gentle means mild or soft
folk is a kind of traditional music

explanation.surface: Soft, traditional tunes suit the aristocracy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes people of good family and breeding, the old upper classes.

clue.text: Managers see drawback in returning stage furniture

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other
returning means the word for stage furniture is read backwards

parts.note: sets are the scenery and furniture on a theatre stage
read as 'draw back', the word draw turned round

explanation.surface: Theatre managers watch someone dragging the scenery back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawback' is not a disadvantage but DRAW turned back, WARD; 'returning' reverses SETS to STES, and 'in' puts WARD inside it. 'see' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewards are people who manage an estate, event or household on behalf of others.

clue.text: A novice intent on making money once

indicators.note: in places the novice and the A inside the canvas shelter

parts.note: a tent is a canvas shelter
L is the learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A beginner set on earning money in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intent' splits as 'in tent': A and L (the learner sign) go inside TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: In the ancient world a talent was a unit of weight and a large sum of money.
